title: Don't truncate, decompose: mean-field dynamics of long-range quantum systems from strongly correlated states
abstract: We challenge the widespread consensus that mean-field theory fails to describe long-range open quantum systems in the presence of symmetry breaking and/or when starting from strongly correlated states (e.g., macroscopic superpositions). While recent literature relies on cumulant expansions to capture such systems, this approach rests on truncations with no clear justification. Here, we show that it is, at best, conceptually redundant in the strong long-range regime. We show that the evolution can be decomposed into, and fully reconstructed from, independent mean-field dynamics. This decomposition generates the entire hierarchy of cumulants and, as a byproduct, identifies---to our knowledge, for the first time---a regime in which cumulant expansions exactly predict low-order cumulants. We illustrate the power of our findings with two applications: we compute the moment generating function for nonequilibrium $\mathcal{Z}_2$ symmetry breaking, and construct states restoring time-translation symmetry in time crystals. In both cases, our method fully reproduces the exact many-body dynamics, which is out of reach of cumulant expansions. Our results reclaim the exactness of mean-field theory, offering a transparent framework for large-scale open quantum systems.
summary: This paper reclaims the validity of mean-field theory for long-range open quantum systems by proposing a decomposition method. It shows that complex dynamics originating from strongly correlated superpositions can be exactly reconstructed from independent, uncoupled mean-field evolutions in the thermodynamic limit. This provides a powerful and transparent framework superior to truncated cumulant expansions.
main_problem: The paper challenges the consensus that mean-field theory fails for long-range open quantum systems, especially when starting from strongly correlated states or undergoing symmetry breaking.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that the evolution of such systems can be fully reconstructed from independent mean-field dynamics, establishing a framework where mean-field theory is exact in the thermodynamic limit.
method: They propose a decomposition method that reconstructs the full quantum evolution by treating it as an ensemble average over individual mean-field evolutions corresponding to the components of a superposition state.
model_or_system: The analysis applies to general long-range interacting quantum systems governed by a quantum master equation, using models like the open LMG model and time crystals. The dynamics are analyzed in the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$).
key_observables: Macroscopic observables (sample means $m^N_\mu$), moment generating functions, and various cumulants (second and third order).
important_parameters: The strong long-range regime, the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$), and the initial state structure (superposition vs. mixture).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that in the large-$N$ limit, quantum superpositions become indistinguishable from classical statistical mixtures, allowing for the decomposition.
figures_summary: Figures compare the evolution of second and third cumulants for specific models (LMG, time-crystal), showing that the proposed decomposed mean-field method accurately reproduces exact dynamics where standard cumulant expansions fail or predict Gaussian approximations incorrectly.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the failure points of standard mean-field theory and cumulant expansions. It then introduces the decomposition framework, proving its equivalence to exact dynamics in the large-$N$ limit for specific state types (superpositions). Finally, it applies this method successfully to compute observables for complex physical models.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical tool to handle non-trivial quantum correlations in open systems where standard approximations fail, offering an exact framework that bridges the gap between mean-field theory and full many-body dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Decomposed mean-field dynamics. (a) We con- sider a strongly correlated state given by a binary macroscopic superposition. At the mean-field level, the two components of the superposition, |φ1⟩and |φ2⟩, are represented by points on the Bloch sphere. Naively applying mean-field theory de- fines the average-state density matrix ϱ and directly evolves it through the mean-field equations, typically resulting in an incorrect dynamics. (b) In our framework, the initial superpo- sition state is exactly decomposed into its components. Each component evolves independently under the mean-field equa- tions (solid arrows), and averaging their evolution yields the exact dynamics (dashed arrow)...
